title: Latency Helix Inspector: per-model/route p50-p95-p99 with streaming vs blocking cohorts
creator: Maya Patel
description: Build a single investigative dashboard (Latency Helix Inspector) that surfaces p50/p95/p99 latency breakouts for every model+route combination and splits traffic by IO mode: streaming vs non-streaming (blocking). This ticket wires tracing hooks and enriches metrics/log pipelines so the board can show cohorted percentiles, tail-fingerprints, and quick links to traces and relevant logs. The goal is to accelerate root cause analysis for route degradations and to provide SREs/Oncall with actionable SLO rollup views.
acceptance_criteria: Dashboard shows p50/p95/p99 per model+route with columns for streaming and non-streaming cohorts
Each row links to a filtered trace search and to the combined log view for that model+route+io_mode
New tracing hook propagates 'io_mode' and 'conversation_shape' as span attributes for all server-side spans
Metrics pipeline emits cohorted histograms/sketches for fast percentile rollups (supports 1m/5m/1h resolutions)
Automated tests for attribute propagation and pipeline tag mappings exist in telemetry repo
Runbook snippet added and Oncall training note published in Confluence
proposed_solution: 1) Add lightweight tracing hook in request router that tags spans with io_mode (streaming|blocking), model_name, route, and conversation_shape buckets (short|medium|long). 2) Enrich request metrics with same tags and switch histogram recording to DDSketch (or HDR) in the metrics agent so p99 can be approximated at ingest. 3) Update log-shipper to add structured fields model/route/io_mode to logs for fast slicing. 4) Build Grafana board using pre-aggregated histogram_rollup metrics and link panels to tracing UI (trace-search URL templates) and Log Explorer queries. 5) Canary the hook on 10% of traffic for 72h and validate coverage and cardinality impact.
implementation_notes: Tracing hook: insert at ingress router (pkg/serve/ingress). Add minimal allocation path and sampling guard to avoid overhead on hot paths.
Metrics: change 'serve_request_duration_seconds' to use DDSketch summary: record with tags {model, route, io_mode, conv_shape}. Backfill aggregation keys in TSDB.
Logs: update log schema in agents to include 'redwood.model' 'redwood.route' 'redwood.io_mode' fields. Ensure redaction rules unchanged.
Cardinality mitigation: quantize conversation_shape into 3 buckets and limit route+model combos to top N via a metrics-allowlist. Emit '_sampled' fallback metric when new combinations appear.
Dashboards: use histogram_rollup_{bucket} series for efficient percentile calculations. If unavailable, compute percentiles via native Grafana sketch plugin.
Testing: unit tests for attribute propagation, integration test that exercises streaming endpoint and asserts metrics + span tags present.
Telemetry infra owners: tag changes in metrics YAML and coordinate with infra-team for retention cost impact.
Perf guardrails: measure 95th token-path CPU overhead in canary; abort if >2% p95 delta.
Docs: add Confluence design doc and link to dashboard JSON and PRs
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (dev): Implement hooks behind feature flag 'latency_helix' and unit tests. Phase 2 (staging): Enable for internal traffic, validate tag coverage, and run cardinality analysis over 48h. Phase 3 (canary): 10% production traffic for 72h; monitor ingestion rate, TSDB cardinality and cost delta. Phase 4 (full): enable for all traffic with allowlist; launch Grafana board and runbook. Phase 5 (observe): 30d review and iterate on buckets/allowlist.
sample_queries: Log Explorer: redwood.model="gpt-7b" AND redwood.route="completions" AND redwood.io_mode="streaming" | sort @timestamp desc
